question: Can you ask for a higher CloudTrail quota?

evidence.quote: CloudTrail has no adjustable quotas.

claim: For an ongoing record of events in your account beyond the past 90 days of Event history, create a trail or a CloudTrail Lake event data store.

claim: CloudTrail publishes log files multiple times an hour, about every 5 minutes, and they contain API calls from services in the account that support CloudTrail.
question: How often does CloudTrail publish log files to the S3 bucket of a trail?

evidence.quote: CloudTrail publishes log files multiple times an hour, about every 5 minutes. These log files contain API calls from services in the account that support CloudTrail.

claim: If a trail is misconfigured, for example the S3 bucket is unreachable, CloudTrail attempts to redeliver the log files for 30 days, and these attempts are subject to standard CloudTrail charges; deleting the trail avoids the charges.
question: For how long does CloudTrail retry delivery to an unreachable S3 bucket, and are the retries charged?

evidence.quote: If you misconfigure your trail (for example, the S3 bucket is unreachable), CloudTrail will attempt to redeliver the log files to your S3 bucket for 30 days, and these attempted-to-deliver events will be subject to standard CloudTrail charges.

claim: AWS CloudTrail Lake closed to new customers starting May 31, 2026; sign-up had to happen before that date, and existing customers can continue to use the service as normal.
question: Can a new customer start using CloudTrail Lake now?

values.display: Existing customers can continue to use the service as normal

evidence.quote: After careful consideration, we decided to close AWS CloudTrail Lake to new customers starting May 31, 2026. If you would like to use CloudTrail Lake, sign up prior to that date. Existing customers can continue to use the service as normal.

note: Old practice questions may name CloudTrail Lake as the answer for SQL queries on events; for new designs the page recommends Amazon CloudWatch.

claim: Only CloudTrail Lake is closed to new customers; CloudTrail itself is fully supported, and your trails, Insights and aggregated events are not affected.
question: Does the CloudTrail Lake closure affect CloudTrail trails and Insights?

values.display: AWS CloudTrail continues to be fully supported
Only AWS CloudTrail Lake is no longer open to new customers

evidence.quote: AWS CloudTrail continues to be fully supported. Only AWS CloudTrail Lake is no longer open to new customers. Your AWS CloudTrail Trails, Insights and Aggregated Events are not affected.

claim: AWS recommends that CloudTrail Lake customers migrate their Lake log data to Amazon CloudWatch.
question: What does AWS recommend instead of CloudTrail Lake?

values.display: migrate your AWS CloudTrail Lake logs data to Amazon CloudWatch

evidence.quote: We recommend that you migrate your AWS CloudTrail Lake logs data to Amazon CloudWatch.

claim: With only account-level event data stores, CloudTrail Lake does not support ingestion for new accounts added to your organization; an organization event data store covers new member accounts.
question: After the closure, which Lake event data stores keep covering new accounts in an organization?

values.display: will not support ingestion for new accounts

evidence.quote: If your AWS Organization has only account-level event data stores, AWS CloudTrail Lake will continue to support those existing accounts, including expansion to new AWS Regions. However, AWS CloudTrail Lake will not support ingestion for new accounts added to your organization.

claim: CloudTrail Lake one-year extendable retention pricing includes the first year of retention with the ingestion cost, and retention can be extended to a maximum of 10 years. This is historical: Lake is closed to new customers.
question: How long could CloudTrail Lake keep events with one-year extendable retention pricing?

values.display: The first year of data retention is included

qualifiers.condition: Recommended for usage under 25 TB a month.

evidence.quote: One-year extendable retention pricing is recommended if your monthly usage is under 25 TB. The first year of data retention is included with the ingestion cost, and you can extend your retention period to a maximum of 10 years.

claim: CloudTrail Lake seven-year retention pricing includes seven years of retention with the ingestion cost, and the retention period cannot be extended past 7 years. This is historical: Lake is closed to new customers.
question: How long could CloudTrail Lake keep events with seven-year retention pricing?

values.display: Seven years of retention are included

qualifiers.condition: Recommended for usage over 25 TB a month.

evidence.quote: Seven-year retention pricing is recommended if your monthly usage exceeds 25 TB. Seven years of retention are included with the ingestion cost, and the retention period cannot be extended past 7 years.
